p: Text prompts pose questions about reviewing a local HTML specification. The video demonstrates sharing the file via an Artifact Share URL, highlighting text with a comment to shorten the project timeline, running a Claude CLI command to apply feedback, showing metrics automatically update on the document at the same URL, and concluding with a logo and CTA card.
Artifact Share allows teams to share AI-generated documents via a single link where review comments can be applied directly by coding agents without changing the URL.

The ad effectively demonstrates the full workflow loop within a concise timeframe. Pacing remains steady and legible on small screens, though the terminal transition is somewhat abrupt. Motion graphics feel functional, and audio supports the beat changes without distraction.

p: ["garbled/illegible microcopy under URL bar (frame1)","motion-blur double-exposure on '3 weeks' stat card obscures text (frame3)","end card shows only logo mark, no visible CTA text or URL"]

The 'wrote checkout-spec.html / Who reviews it?' hook and the comment-bubble-to-edited-numbers beat (6 weeks/$38k → 3 weeks) clearly dramatize the human-points/agent-edits value prop, which is the strongest part of the ad. However the transition frame has a visible glitchy text smear on the key '3 weeks' stat, and the metadata line under the URL is unreadable, both reading as render artifacts rather than stylistic choices. The ad also ends cold on a bare logo icon with no 'Try it free — artifactshare.com' copy visible in the sampled frames, so the CTA doesn't land without narration/on-screen text elsewhere in the cut.
